title: Stucco vs. Brick in Houston: Cost, Upkeep and Painting
description: Brick costs more up front but needs almost no upkeep unless painted. Stucco is smooth and versatile but needs crack repair and repainting in Houston's clay soil and humidity. Here's how they compare.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: brick usually costs more to install but needs very little upkeep as long as it stays unpainted. Stucco gives a smooth, seamless look and takes color well, but in the Houston area it needs regular crack repair, sealing and repainting. Our shifting clay soil and humidity are hard on rigid stucco. Many Fort Bend homes mix the two, with brick on the lower story and stucco or siding above.

Stucco: Pros and Cons

Pros

  • Smooth, seamless look that suits modern and Mediterranean styles

  • Takes almost any paint color, so it's easy to update

  • Usually less expensive to install than full brick

Cons

  • Cracks. Fort Bend's expansive clay soil swells when wet and shrinks in drought, and that movement shows up as hairline cracks in rigid stucco.

  • Moisture. Unsealed cracks let water in, which can lead to stains, mildew and damage behind the surface.

  • Ongoing maintenance. Painted stucco needs crack repair and repainting on a regular cycle to stay sealed.

See stucco repairs, stucco maintenance and stucco painting.

Brick: Pros and Cons

Pros

  • Very durable and fire-resistant

  • Unpainted brick needs almost no maintenance beyond occasional cleaning and mortar repair

  • Classic look that holds its appeal for buyers

Cons

  • Higher installation cost

  • Fewer color options unless you paint or limewash it

  • Painting brick is a commitment. Once painted, it needs repainting over time, and removing paint from brick is difficult.

Painting Each One

Stucco is porous and textured. It needs cracks filled with flexible products, a clean surface, and coating sprayed on and back-rolled into the texture. Brick should be cleaned and fully dry, and it needs a breathable masonry coating so moisture can escape. Limewash is an alternative that soaks in and weathers naturally instead of forming a film. Learn more about brick painting.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which is better in Houston, stucco or brick?

Brick generally holds up better with less maintenance in our soil and climate. Stucco can look great and last well if cracks are kept sealed and it's repainted on schedule.

Why does stucco crack in Fort Bend County?

Mostly because the clay soil underneath swells and shrinks with moisture, moving the foundation and the rigid stucco with it.

Does painting brick increase home value?

It can freshen a dated exterior, but it adds a maintenance commitment. Read whether painting before selling is worth it.
